cases.why: The control every other case here is measured against.
Reading a pull request is Auto. An agent never decides for itself that a change is ready to land; reading whether it is, is not that decision.
Until 2026-07-28 this matched no gate at all — the matcher prefix-matched the whole command string, so every Gated outward action here was defeated by typing anything in front of it.
A newline is a command separator. The Bash tool receives multi-line scripts constantly, and this was the plainest escape of the eight.
The hook peels exactly one shell wrapper.
Two claims that each held and did not compose: unwrapping was anchored at the start of the command, so a wrapper that was not first was never unwrapped.
Closed at #71, 2026-08-24. Every shell rule inherited the fix at once, which is why it is asserted on every one of them rather than only on the rule the issue quoted.

Open by decision, and shared by every shell rule. A named table of command prefixes has no natural edge — `nice`, `time`, `nohup`, `timeout`, `command`, `stdbuf`, `doas` — and one omission buys the false confidence a hole list exists to deny.
The other half of the leader hole: `commandSegments` reads a list of separators, not a grammar, so a word occupying the head position hides the command behind it.
